title: A company town for potash
text: In 1913, the British-owned Consolidated Gold Fields of South Africa founded the American Trona Corporation, which set up Trona as a company-run town. In 1914, the Trona Railway opened a 31-mile line from Trona to the Southern Pacific junction at Searles Station. The railway was built to bring the company's potash to an interchange with the Southern Pacific. A heavily financed refinery at Trona was completed in October 1916.
